arguments.command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /root/.openclaw/workspace
# Determine likely user home(s)
HOMES=()
if [ -d /home ]; then
  while IFS= read -r -d '' d; do HOMES+=("$d"); done < <(find /home -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -print0 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
# also consider root
HOMES+=("/root")

# Mail client / mail-store directory patterns to check
patterns=(
  ".thunderbird" ".mozilla-thunderbird" ".config/thunderbird" ".config/Thunderbird"
  ".evolution" ".config/evolution" ".local/share/evolution"
  ".kmail" ".local/share/local-mail" ".local/share/kmail" ".local/share/akonadi" ".config/akonadi" ".config/kmail2" ".config/kmail"
  ".config/geary" ".local/share/geary"
  ".config/mailspring" ".config/Mailspring"
  ".config/Mail" ".config/gnome-multi-writer" 
  ".config/mutt" ".mutt" ".config/neomutt" ".offlineimap" ".mbsyncrc" ".isync" ".maildir" "Maildir" "mail" "Mail"
  ".local/share/mail" ".local/share/Mail" ".local/share/maildir" ".local/share/Maildir"
  ".config/protonmail" ".config/protonmail-bridge" ".config/ProtonMail" ".config/ProtonMailBridge"
  ".config/gmail" 
)

# Check directories/files presence
printf "{" 
first_home=1
for home in "${HOMES[@]}"; do
  [ -d "$home" ] || continue
  found=()
  for p in "${patterns[@]}"; do
    if [ -e "$home/$p" ]; then
      found+=("$p")
    fi
  done
  if [ ${#found[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
    [ $first_home -eq 1 ] || printf ","
    first_home=0
    printf "\n  %s: [" "\"$home\""
    first=1
    for f in "${found[@]}"; do
      [ $first -eq 1 ] || printf ", "
      first=0
      printf "%s" "\"$f\""
    done
    printf "]"
  fi
done
printf "\n}\n"

arguments.command:
cd / 
# Search for Outlook archive formats and mbox-like files. Limit to likely homes.
search_roots="/home /root"
# Find PST/OST
find $search_roots -type f \( -iname "*.pst" -o -iname "*.ost" \) -print 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/FILE: /'

# Find common mbox filenames (no extension) and *.mbox
find $search_roots -type f \( -iname "*.mbox" -o -iname "mbox" -o -iname "inbox" -o -iname "sent" -o -iname "archive" -o -iname "mail" \) -print 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/CANDIDATE: /'

cd / 
# Heuristic: search for files with 'From ' mbox delimiter in first line among reasonably-sized files under likely mail dirs
search_roots="/home /root"
# restrict to typical mail storage directories
find $search_roots -type d \( -iname "*mail*" -o -iname "*thunderbird*" -o -iname "*evolution*" -o -iname "*geary*" \) -print 2>/dev/null | head -n 200 | while read d; do
  find "$d" -type f -size +1k -size -200M 2>/dev/null | while read f; do
    # check first 5 bytes for 'From '
    head -c 5 "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^From " && echo "MBOX?: $f"
  done
done

[Sat 2026-05-09 05:10 UTC] Calculate the total size of the mail archive files to determine transfer time.

arguments.command:
cd / 
# Sum sizes for any discovered archive files (pst/ost/mbox). Re-run a focused find and compute totals.
search_roots="/home /root"
files=$(find $search_roots -type f \( -iname "*.pst" -o -iname "*.ost" -o -iname "*.mbox" -o -iname "mbox" \) 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$files" ]; then
  echo "TOTAL_BYTES=0"
  echo "TOTAL_HUMAN=0B"
  exit 0
fi
# bytes
bytes=$(printf "%s\n" "$files" | xargs -I{} stat -c %s "{}" 2>/dev/null | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
# human
human=$(awk -v b="$bytes" 'BEGIN{
  split("B KB MB GB TB PB",u," ");
  i=1; v=b;
  while(v>=1024 && i<6){v/=1024; i++}
  if(i==1) printf("%d%s", b, u[i]); else printf("%.2f%s", v, u[i]);
}')

printf "TOTAL_BYTES=%s\nTOTAL_HUMAN=%s\n" "$bytes" "$human"
# also list files
printf "FILES:\n%s\n" "$files"
